notes: Corrected: the supplied and at t018 was carried on ἔπειτα as a rule 29 helper. Rule 98 governs an asyndetic seam between two like constituents both rendered alike and makes the juncture added under rule 5, and it says in terms that rule 29's compound-numeral juncture is not a general licence and that rule 88's protection reaches only a circumstantial participle converted into a coordinate finite clause. The Greek coordinates πρότερον … ἔπειτα with no conjunction, so nothing licenses the word.
ἔχει ἀνάγκην is collapsed into needeth under rule 73, with the source head on the noun the English verb realizes.
The italicized second sins is added under rule 103, ἁμαρτιῶν having already been spent at t017; the unit note concedes the rule 15 reading.
The two added units of this verse rest on different rules — rule 103 for the repeated sins, rule 98 for the asyndetic juncture — and neither is decided by the ASV's italics under rule 11.
